reader_notes: Reads as authentic Swedish sakprosa throughout: register, period vocabulary and idiom are convincing (vinterföre, dagsverkena, karvstock, gå i dagen, avsalu, hålla elden vid makt, jämkades). Nothing reads as translationese, and the byline register (kulturskribent) fits the museum-reconstruction ending.

Friction 1 (punctuation, repeated): fronted conditional clauses lack the comma Swedish normally takes. 'Möter den brända stenen sedan vatten börjar den sjuda...' made me re-read the clause boundary; same pattern in 'svalnade ugnen i förtid var satsen förstörd'. Comprehension survives, but an editor would insert commas.

Friction 2 (numbers, soft): the text says 'En enda bränning slukade mer ved än ett hushåll annars gjorde av med på ett år', then the reconstruction has 'tretton kubikmeter björk' stacked for the coming burn. Thirteen cubic metres is low against a 19th-century household's annual firewood, so the two figures sit slightly oddly together. Not contradictory on the page (the reconstruction kiln need not match a historical charge, and the pile is not stated to be the whole supply), but it is the one number a careful reader pauses on.

Chemistry and history check out for a general reader: calcination near 1000 degrees driving off carbon dioxide, slaking to a fine white powder, lime mortar as the dominant use, continuous railway-side kilns plus cement undercutting a neighbour co-op late in the century.

q:1 A — 'Möter den brända stenen sedan vatten börjar den sjuda, spricker och faller sönder till ett fint vitt mjöl.' D is the sharp distractor (sand blending is real but not 'medan den ännu sjöd'); B and C are unsupported.
q:2 D — 'En ugn var för stor för ett enskilt hushåll. Den restes och brändes av ett ugnslag – en handfull grannar...' C is directly contradicted by 'Det mesta av kalken gick till avsalu'.

q:3 B — binäring that gave cash, then 'Mot seklets slut tappade ugnslagen sin marknad' with prices falling below what a lag could meet. A contradicted by 'Framför allt var det dit kalken gick: till murningen'; C reverses the railway's role; D contradicted by 'Berget var däremot sällan något bekymmer'.

q:4 C — the seventy-odd remains include successive generations: 'inte sällan flera i rad utmed samma sluttning, äldre ugnar som övergivits när skogen omkring dem huggits ut, och som ersatts av en yngre ugn längre bort', reinforced by each kiln firing only every second or third year. D is explicitly denied ('går inte att avgöra utan utgrävning'); B is denied by the museum using Gillervall's uppmätningar as förlaga; A overreads 'gränsen mellan inägor och utmark' (a farm/village boundary) as parish boundaries.
No cross-question leakage: q:2 and q:3 both touch the binäring theme, but neither stem or option set gives away the other's key, and nothing is answerable without reading the passage.
